FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED (Postgres 9.5+) lets concurrent transactions claim distinct rows from a candidate set without blocking on rows already locked by another in-flight transaction -- the standard non-blocking job-queue claim pattern. The lock is bound to the transaction: a crashed claimant's transaction never commits, so Postgres releases the lock and the row becomes claimable again automatically. Caveat: it only protects the claimed rows themselves; any invariant spanning MULTIPLE rows or external state (e.g. an external API call) still needs application-level care -- exactly why this phase forbids the reconciler from calling SendGrid inside or after its claim (classification-only).
